answer:
The Diversity in Pottery Form collapses while the Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneously in the 17th century BCE (the CE -1700 / 1700 BCE bin). Attribution convention: the event is dated to the century that BEGINS at the 100-year point carrying the new (collapsed) value — the 1700 BCE point is the start of the 17th century BCE.

Evidence: At the 100-year transition from 1800 BCE to 1700 BCE, PotteryForm falls from 0.74 to -1.13 (Δ = -1.87, its steepest collapse and all-time low, then flat at -1.13 for the next 1,200 years), while PotteryDecoration rises from -0.48 to 0.97 (Δ = +1.45, continuing to 1.53 by 1000 BCE). This is the ONLY bin in the series where Form declines and Decoration rises together, and it is the largest Form drop by a wide margin (runner-up is CE -2800, Δ=-0.90, which is paired with a Decoration DROP of -0.69). The result is confirmed independently by capital.csv (ZKeform, Zkeverz).

payload.hypothesis: In the 17th century BCE (the CE -1700 / 1700 BCE 100-year bin), the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses while the Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneously. Specifically, from 1800 BCE to 1700 BCE the PotteryForm Z-score falls from +0.74 to -1.13 (a -1.87 collapse to its all-time low, where it remains flat for the following 1,200 years) while the PotteryDecoration Z-score rises from -0.48 to +0.97 (a +1.45 increase, continuing to +1.53 by 1000 BCE). This is the only 100-year bin in the series where Form declines and Decoration rises together, it is by far the steepest Form collapse, and it is independently confirmed by the capital.csv ZKeform/Zkeverz series.
payload.workflow: 1) Parsed time_series_data.csv (3,601 rows, CE -4100..-500, 1-yr grid) and capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300..500, 100-yr grid, decimal-comma format converted to dots). 2) Extracted the true 100-year resolution of the pottery Z-scores: the raw PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration columns are populated at only 37 evenly spaced 100-yr points (the _inter columns are pure linear interpolation and were not used for detection). 3) Computed first differences (dForm, dDeco) between consecutive 100-yr bins and flagged bins where Form_down (dForm<0) and Deco_up (dDeco>0) hold simultaneously. 4) Selected the bin with the steepest sustained PotteryForm collapse (largest negative dForm, excluding the -4100->-4000 baseline artifact) that is paired with a simultaneous Decoration increase, and verified the post-event Form level stays at its minimum (sustained, not transient). 5) Mapped the selected CE value to a calendar century (CE v = |v| BCE; Nth century BCE begins at 100*N BCE) and attributed the event to the century beginning at the point carrying the new value. 6) Cross-checked against capital.csv ZKeform/Zkeverz: all 36 shared bins (excluding the BCE-500 artifact row) match exactly. Executed script: analysis.py.
